messages:
sarah (AE): Just got off a call with Greenbank — POC needs strict EU + Canada data residency. They said no APAC/US subprocessors may touch customer data during the POC. Also need BYO-KMS for Canada and a private peering path. Can we do this for a 30‑day POC?

mike (SE): Re: yes we can restrict routing to specific regions but need to confirm the subprocessor footprint. For hosted API we can pin requests to EU & CA regions with regional endpoints. For Dedicated/Private we can do tenant pinning + network peering.

leah (Presales): Pricing note — if they want Dedicated reserved capacity for consistent throughput in eu + ca we should run a short cost model. Ballpark: small dedicated pool (2x A10G equiv) + BYOK support will be a tiered add-on. I can draft a quick quote if we confirm ops constraints. :money_with_wings:

raj (Infra): Quick facts: our infra uses underlying cloud regions and a handful of subprocessors for telemetry/monitoring and backups. Need to confirm which subprocessors are in APAC/US. If customer forbids any APAC/US subprocessor involvement we may need Private deployment (control plane in their VPC) or a Dedicated contract that excludes certain managed services.

ryan (NetOps): For the tenant pin + peering, config snippet we usually share:```yaml
routing:
  allowed_regions: ["europe-west3","northamerica-northeast1"]
  tenant_pin: true
  peering: 
    - peer: customer-vpc
      routes: ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  subprocessor_blocklist: ["apac-monitoring-1","us-telemetry-2"]
```
This enforces region affinity on the serving path. For BYO-KMS we need the KMS key ARN and a short IAM handoff doc.

sarah (AE): Greenbank asked for a single doc that says: 1) which subprocessors touch inference requests and where 2) how we guarantee no egress to APAC/US during POC 3) BYO-KMS in Canada steps 4) estimated monthly cost for a limited Dedicated footprint. Can someone own assembling that today?

mike (SE): I can own the tech doc. Action items for me: 1) confirm subprocessor list & region mapping with legal-bot 2) capture routing config + examples (above) 3) list deployment options (Hosted pinned endpoints vs Dedicated vs Private). Expect a draft in ~4 hours.

legal-bot: Subprocessor inventory: https://redwood.internal/subprocessors (internal) — current footprint: majority infra providers in EU + NA, telemetry vendor has APAC presence (apac-monitoring-1). For strict POC we can provide an attestation and options: a) disable telemetry for that tenant b) Private deployment.

leah (Presales): I'll prep a 30-day proof-of-concept quote variant: hosted pinned endpoints (no telemetry) vs small Dedicated commit. Need the SKU for BYO-KMS add-on and the delta for peering egress.

raj (Infra): Note: disabling telemetry reduces some observability — we should document what we lose. Also backups metadata may still be in US by default for some managed services; need ops approval to restrict backups to EU/CA for that tenant.

sarah (AE): Perfect — greenbank expects a one-pager they can sign for the POC today. Mike + Leah can you sync offline and I'll update the customer? 

mike (SE): Yup — ping me when you have the BYOK key info from the customer. I'll include the config snippet and a short playbook for ops to lock down subprocessors.

leah (Presales): I'll attach two draft quotes to the thread when ready. ETA 3h. :hourglass: 

ryan (NetOps): FYI if we do private deployment we'll need an ops runbook for teardown after 30 days — I'll draft it.

sarah (AE): Thanks all — marking as high priority. I'll follow up with Greenbank to get BYOK details and whether they will allow any managed-service subprocessors in NA for logs.

mike (SE): One more thing — customer asked whether model weights ever leave region during autoscaling. Short answer: we can pin model host placement to regions configured in the routing policy; I will add a short section on model residency + warm cache behavior.

sarah (AE): Great. If we have the one-pager + quote today we can move to sign-off and schedule the POC next week. :rocket:
